subject: GPU sprint readiness: late-stage AstraGrid deal
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: GPU sprint readiness for AstraGrid (late-stage)

Team,

Quick context: AstraGrid (DEAL-7684) is in final procurement. Legal and procurement want a firm start window and an SOW; Sales is asking for a 21-day soft-hold while they finalize signatures. Before we commit anything I need a runway assessment and a short recommendation on a soft-hold approach that preserves capacity for our other customers. Key ask: can we cover a 12-month dedicated deployment expected to ramp to ~8xA100-equivalent sustained (peaks up to 12 concurrent allocated GPUs) starting calendar Q1 2027 if we place a soft hold now?

What I need from Ops/Capacity:
- Current available pool by region (us-west/us-east) and expected reclamation windows over next 90 days.
- Feasible soft-hold duration (how long we can mark GPUs as reserved without blocking production scheduling).
- If shortfall, suggested mitigations (mixed-instance plan, preemptible fallback, cross-region routing).
- Any SLA implications for a rapid ramp to 12 GPUs.

Attachments: draft SOW (SOW-AstraGrid-v0.3.pdf) and an initial commercial deck in Drive link.

Timeline: need a concise memo and recommended playbook by EOD Friday (11/27) so we can feed it into the MIP for pricing and legal.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GPU sprint readiness for AstraGrid (late-stage)

Ben et al,

Quick scan attached (fleet-snapshot-20261125.csv). Short version:
- We have a ~14 GPU-equivalent buffer in us-west available for reservation windows starting mid-December if we do a soft hold (fleet mix today: 6xA100-80GB, 4xL40-48GB, remainder older GPUs).
- Pure A100-only allocation to get 8xA100 sustained would require rebalancing — estimated 5–7 days to stage and migrate nodes if we prioritize this deal.
- Alternative: mixed profile (6xA100 + 4xL40 configured with quantization/latency tuning) can reach target token throughput with an acceptable tail-latency impact (we estimate +15–25ms p95).
- Soft-hold policy recommendation: allow a 21-day soft hold with throttled allocation (we can tag GPUs and avoid committing them to on-demand until contract signed). After 21 days we require either a firm commit or release policy to avoid blocking growth.

Risks/notes:
- If another priority enterprise opportunity requires immediate A100s in the same window, we need a clause for priority escalation (ops-led manual override).
- Networking (cross-region) will add 10–20ms depending on routing; worth checking AstraGrid's latency tolerance.

Attaching fleet snapshot and a short runbook fragment.

Monica
Monica Patel
Capacity Planning Lead
Redwood Inference
Attachments: fleet-snapshot-20261125.csv

Clara / team,

Looping you in on our internal capacity scan and an ask for a short confirmation so ops can place a soft hold. Attached is the current SOW draft (SOW-AstraGrid-v0.3.pdf) and an internal fleet snapshot. To help us finalize the soft-hold we'll need you to confirm the expected production profile below:
- Peak concurrent allocated GPUs: expected 12
- Average sustained allocated GPUs: expected 8 (first 90 days)
- Typical request pattern: bursty inference (intermittent batch jobs) + sustained low-latency API.
- Target latency p95: <= 120ms (region: US-West preferred)

Proposed next step: 30-minute call tomorrow to align on workload and finalize a mutual action plan. If you confirm these numbers we will request a 21-day soft hold on a handful of A100-equivalent nodes pending signature.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: GPU sprint readiness for AstraGrid (late-stage)

Ben / team,

Thanks for the heads-up and the SOW. We confirm the profile roughly matches our expectations:
- Peak concurrent: 10–12 GPUs (likely 12 in peak tests)
- Sustained: ~7–8 GPUs after roll-out
- Workload: mixed real-time inference with scheduled nightly batch fine-tuning (peaks in early morning PST)
- Latency: p95 target 110–120ms (US-West preferred)

We agree to a 21-day soft hold to allow legal to finish signatures. Please note procurement will expect clear terms on failure to deliver (ramp SLAs) and a fallback routing plan if hardware rebalancing is needed.

Proposed call: Friday 11/27 at 11:00 AM PST (30m).

Regards,
Clara Torres
CTO, AstraGrid
